title: Opinionated retry shim and idempotency migration tooling for SDKs
creator: Anika Patel
description: Problem: Customer apps embedding Redwood SDKs see inconsistent retry behavior across languages. Some calls retry aggressively causing duplicates; others never retry leading to transient failures surfaced to end users. We need an opinionated, minimal-surface compatibility layer (a 'retry shim') across Python/TypeScript/Go that provides sensible defaults, clear idempotency key semantics, a documented retryable error taxonomy, and a migration path for existing clients.
design_notes: The shim will live inside each SDK as a thin policy layer that composes with existing transport layers (HTTP/gRPC). Design goals: 1) Safe-by-default: non-destructive operations must not be retried unless caller opts-in or an idempotency key is provided; 2) Consistent developer ergonomics across languages; 3) Minimal friction for users to opt into stricter retry behavior; 4) Backward-compatible: defaults should preserve prior semantics for existing customers unless they opt in to 'opinionated mode'.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDKs expose a single cross-language config object: retryPolicy and idempotencyOptions
2) Default retryPolicy applied in GA corresponds to documented parameters (see sdk_defaults) and preserves prior non-opinionated behavior unless opt-in flag is set
3) Idempotency header and TTL behavior implemented consistently across Python/TS/Go
4) A migration runbook is published and includes a GitHub migration helper script and a CLI checker for server call sites
5) End-to-end tests for retry behavior added to SDK e2e matrix and pass on CI for all three languages
6) Telemetry events emitted for suppressed retries and idempotency mismatches to aid debugging
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Prototype shim in TypeScript SDK only. Provide toggled 'opinionated' config flag. Implement default backoff and idempotency key header 'X-Redwood-Idempotency' with TTL metadata in SDK local cache.
Phase 2 (2 weeks): Port shim to Python and Go. Add language-native ergonomics: contextmanager for Python, middleware builder for Go, and fluent builder in TypeScript.
Phase 3 (1 week): Add e2e tests, CI matrix, and a migration CLI tool that scans codebases for uses of non-idempotent endpoints.
Phase 4 (1 week): Release opt-in beta, collect telemetry, run compatibility checks with internal users and early customers, then flip opt-in guidance to recommended in docs.
Implementation notes: Keep transport-agnostic logic isolated; all HTTP/gRPC status mapping must be in a single source-of-truth mapping file per SDK to reduce drift.
migration_runbook: Step 0: Read the migration guide in Confluence (link in linked_artifacts).
Step 1: Add SDK opt-in flag 'enableOpinionatedRetries=true' in staging only. Run integration tests targeting known flaky endpoints.

Step 2: For any failures, inspect SDK telemetry event 'rw.retry.suppressed' and check for missing idempotency keys. If call is not idempotent, either supply an idempotency key or mark operation as no-retry.
Step 3: Use provided migration CLI to scan repositories. The CLI will flag usage of endpoints in the 'non-idempotent-by-default' list and produce per-call suggestions.
Step 4: Gradually enable in production via a canary rollout to 5% of traffic. Monitor error rate and duplicate side-effects dashboard.
sdk_defaults: Global design: Explicit opt-in for aggressive retries. Default policy is conservative and mirrors current behavior to avoid surprises.
Default retryPolicy parameters (opinionated mode): initial_backoff_ms=100, max_backoff_ms=5000, multiplier=2.0, jitter=full (randomized), max_attempts=5
Safe-only mode: max_attempts=1 (no retries) unless idempotency key or explicit allow_retries=true provided
Header conventions: X-Redwood-Idempotency for HTTP; metadata 'redwood-idempotency' for gRPC. SDKs also accept 'idempotency_key' parameter in call helpers.
TTL: SDK retains locally generated idempotency tokens for 24 hours by default and will resend token on transport retries only; server-side TTL recommended 48 hours.
Streaming note: Retries for streaming endpoints are disabled by default; streaming resume tokens (if supported) must be implemented explicitly by service and SDK.
Language ergonomics: Python context manager support (with client.retry_policy(...)), TypeScript fluent builder (client.withRetry(...)), Go functional option (client.WithRetryPolicy(...)).
retryable_error_taxonomy: Retryable transient errors (safe to retry with idempotency or for read-only ops): TCP/EPIPE, ECONNRESET, DNS failures, HTTP 429, HTTP 503, HTTP 502 (gateway), gRPC UNAVAILABLE, gRPC RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED
Conditionally retryable (only when idempotency key present or operation marked idempotent): HTTP 500, HTTP 409 (if server indicates idempotent conflict metadata), gRPC ABORTED
Non-retryable by default: HTTP 400, 401, 403, 404, gRPC INVALID_ARGUMENT, PERMISSION_DENIED, NOT_FOUND

Streaming-specific: For long-lived streaming sessions, only safe operation is to attempt connection-level reconnects; application-level message replay requires server-provided resume tokens. SDK will expose resumeToken plumbing but will not auto-retry message deliveries without explicit resume semantics.
streaming_constraints: Do not auto-retry streaming request bodies that mutate server state unless idempotency/resume semantics defined by service.
Expose cancellable async iterators for Python/TS and context.Context cancellation for Go to let callers abort retries immediately.
Provide 'resumeToken' carrier in streaming response metadata and helper utilities to persist resumeToken between reconnections.
Add a 'stream_unrecoverable' event to telemetry when resume is impossible so SRE can triage state loss.
examples: Python example: with client.operation(idempotency_key='op-123') as resp: # context manager applies idempotency and retry shim\n\tresult = resp.execute()
TypeScript example: const client = new RedwoodClient().withRetry({enabled:true, maxAttempts:5}); await client.createInvoice({..}, {idempotencyKey: 'inv-789'});

Go example: c := NewClient(WithRetryPolicy(DefaultOpinionatedPolicy())); ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second); defer cancel(); resp, err := c.CreateCharge(ctx, req, WithIdempotencyKey("chg-456"))
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with SDK owners (Python/TS/Go). Agreed on 'opinionated mode' opt-in approach.
2026-02-18: TypeScript prototype implemented. Basic header wiring and jittered backoff added. First flaky integration tests pass in CI.
2026-02-25: Design review with Security and SRE. Security requested explicit KMS guidance for idempotency key generation when keys are persisted; added to linked_artifacts.
2026-03-03: Python port scaffolded; added contextmanager surface. Found language-specific nuance: asyncio cancellation requires explicit task shield logic—wrote test cases.
2026-03-09: Go middleware implemented. Gave demo to Platform team; they requested extra telemetry on suppressed retries and a debug flag to log idempotency headers.
reviews: PM feedback (Jared Kim): Favor clarity in docs — call out exactly which endpoints are non-idempotent-by-default and include migration checklist.
Design feedback (Lina Zhou): Suggest making TTL configurable per client instance and exposing hook for custom idempotency key generator.
Security review (Sasha Lebedev): For persisted idempotency tokens, document encryption-in-transit and at-rest requirements and do not recommend storing tokens indefinitely.
SRE feedback (Mateo Alvarez): Add duplicate-detection dashboard and an incident playbook entry for duplicate side-effects; recommended adding a sampling flag for telemetry to bound costs.
